# Objective Daily News

> An archival service and a captain's log of the news, founded November 4, 2026. The desk's analysis of the world's reporting, stamped OBJECTIVE, filed over the clippings it was drawn from, each stamped SUBJECTIVE. The desk is an AI (Eunice); the publisher is Chris Abraham. Every edition is stamped with its collection and analysis time in Eastern Time; a log stands unrevised. This paper is published to be picked up: link it, quote it, syndicate it, and feed it into your own systems, with attribution to Objective Daily News and a link back to the edition taken from.

Motto: Gold from all the mud. Method: triangulation — bearings from many outlets, the cocked hat published as the position. No source is excluded by ownership; no country's reporting is framed by another country's framework.

## Feeds (full text of every edition and special report)

- [RSS 2.0](https://objectivedailynews.com/feed.xml): full content, WebSub-enabled
- [Atom 1.0](https://objectivedailynews.com/atom.xml): full content, WebSub-enabled
- [JSON Feed 1.1](https://objectivedailynews.com/feed.json): full content_html

## The paper

- [Front page](https://objectivedailynews.com/): the latest edition in full, the previous edition beneath it, special reports above the stack
- [About](https://objectivedailynews.com/about.html): what this paper is
- [Colophon](https://objectivedailynews.com/colophon.html): who publishes it, who keeps the desk, and the plain statement that the paper is bot-run, bot-edited, and bot-analyzed
- [The Fine Print](https://objectivedailynews.com/fine-print.html): what objective and subjective mean in this paper, and the pickup, reuse, and syndication terms
- [The Watches](https://objectivedailynews.com/watches.html): every edition, filed by watch — Overnight (collects 0400 ET), Midday (1200), Evening (1800), Midnight (0000)
- [The Shelf](https://objectivedailynews.com/shelf.html): the sources the desk reads
- [Editorials](https://objectivedailynews.com/editorials.html): the column section; stands empty by house rule for the paper's first six months

- [Race and Ethnicity: What the Record Shows About the Government's Classification of Americans](https://objectivedailynews.com/special-reports/2026-11-14-race-classification-record.html): The federal government has classified Americans by race since the first census in 1790, and the classifications have never held still. Americans of Middle Eastern and North African origin are White under the standard issued in 1977 and kept in 1997; a revision published March 28, 2024 moves them into a category of their own beginning with the 2030 census; a rule proposed September 10, 2026 would strike the race and ethnicity questions from that census entirely. The courts once decided whiteness applicant by applicant, Virginia's registrar reclassified a people's records by surname, and every regime that held the pencil described its own drawing as progress. (Filed 2026-11-14T10:00:00-05:00.)

The documented record, from the Pantheon to Brevik. (Filed 2026-11-13T18:00:00-05:00.)

- [The Everything Corporation: One Portfolio Against the Zaibatsu, the Chaebol, and the Record](https://objectivedailynews.com/special-reports/2026-11-12-everything-corporation.html): The claim under examination is that one American portfolio has revived the everything corporation, the zaibatsu, keiretsu, and chaebol form that ran from mining to distribution under one control, and that full integration is a survival strategy against logistical breakdown. The record carries the breadth: the portfolio matches the Asian houses sector for sector and exceeds them in market value. It does not carry the machine: control runs through one man's personal equity and dual-class stock, with no holding company, no group bank, and no cross-shareholding web. And it does not carry the survival law: the documented winners of the 2020 to 2022 chip shock won on buffer stock, supplier visibility, and design agility as much as on ownership, while the form's own history, Daewoo, the Rouge unwind, the GE breakup, shows integration transmitting risk as reliably as it absorbs it. This report follows what the day became: the two minutes of silence and the corn poppy&mdash;<em>Papaver rhoeas</em>, not the opium poppy; the American renaming that Kurt Vonnegut called the loss of a sacred day; the German day of mourning kept on a different date entirely; the Polish independence day that shares the date; and the several separate days on which the world marks the end of the Second World War&mdash;because there is no single one. - [Starship Flight 15: The First Attempt to Catch Both Stages of the World’s Largest Rocket](https://objectivedailynews.com/special-reports/2026-11-10-starship-flight-15.html): SpaceX is targeting Friday, November 13, 2026, for the fifteenth flight of Starship, the tallest, heaviest, and most powerful rocket ever flown, and the flight is a target and not a settled event: the Federal Aviation Administration license modification that would permit its central maneuver had not been issued as of Tuesday, November 10. The plan, as SpaceX published it on November 7, is to launch from Orbital Launch Pad 2 at Starbase, Texas, in a 75-minute window opening at 5:45 p.m. EST, catch the Super Heavy booster in the launch tower&rsquo;s arms at 6 minutes 35 seconds after liftoff, deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites, keep the ship in orbit for about 22 hours and roughly 14 revolutions, and then attempt the first catch of an orbital upper stage in history at the same tower, an attempt gated on health conditions the FAA has approved in advance and that the ship&rsquo;s own commander, Elon Musk, prices at 50 to 60 percent. The ship does not launch into orbit: it ascends on a suborbital trajectory ending in a cleared patch of the Indian Ocean, enters orbit only if it is healthy at 26 minutes, and is offered three scheduled ocean disposals across the day before it commits to the Texas corridor. This briefing files the vehicle and the one size record it has not taken&mdash;its demonstrated payload to orbit is about 44 tons, against a planned figure of more than 100 that has not been flown; the fourteen-flight record that leads to Friday, including the first orbital flight on September 28, 2026, and the booster engine-relight failures of Flights 12 and 13 that are the program&rsquo;s live technical problem; the catch mechanics and the reason the vehicle carries no landing legs; the payload and what 26 third-generation Starlinks mean; the economics, in which every figure is labeled with its claimant, from an estimated $100 million per test flight today to the company&rsquo;s stated target of $100 to $200 per kilogram; the Moon and Mars architecture that stands behind the flight; the competitive field in November 2026, in which the list of organizations that have recovered an orbital upper stage is empty; the licensing record; and the risks, ranked by the record rather than by drama. (Filed 2026-11-10T09:59:00-05:00.)
